To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have synthesized a new class of regenerable radical-trapping antioxidants that are based on the combination of a thiophenol moiety with a disulfide bridge and that we have identified a novel mechanism of antioxidant regeneration that involves a telluride group.
the new thiophenolic radical-trapping antioxidants are regenerable and show a higher antioxidant activity than α-tocpherol.
we have developed a new class of regenerable thiophenol antioxidants based on the use of a tellurium atom in the ortho-position to the thiophenol group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new regenerable thiophenolic radical-trapping antioxidants.
the synthesis and evaluation of novel regenerable thiophenolic radical-trapping antioxidants.
the synthesis and evaluation of a novel class of regenerable thiophenolic radical-trapping antioxidants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thiophenolic radical-trapping antioxidants described herein are promising candidates for the protection of lipids against peroxyl radical attack.
the thiophenol generated by the in situ reduction of the disulfide is the actual radical scavenger, which is in accordance with the results of the kinetic studies.
the thiophenols are better antioxidants than their disulfide precursors, and the best thiophenol was the one derived from 7c.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tellurium atom can be used as a convenient handle for the synthesis of novel, regenerable antioxidants, which are more effective than α-tocopheryl acetate.
the thiyl radical formed by the reduction of the thiophenols with TCEP is a more effective radical-trapping antioxidant than α-tocophenol, which is in agreement with the literature.
the alkyltelluro group is an effective and regenerable radical-trapping group for thiophenolic antioxidants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the alkyltelluro group is an effective protecting group for the o-, m- and p-thiophenol moieties, and that the corresponding thiophenic radicals generated by reduction of the disulfides are excellent peroxyl radical scavengers.

thiophenols are excellent peroxyl radical scavengers, and the use of a suitable reductant in combination with the appropriate diphenyl disulfide can result in the development of novel regenerable antioxidants.
the thiophenolic antioxidants were more efficient in the presence of TCEP than α-tocopheryl acetate (α-TocAc) or α-Toc, the latter of which was found to be less effective than the former.
